title: Reference-values manifest
description: The payload of an environment's reference-values manifest: a compact JWS (ES256, header { alg, kid }) signed with the environment's manifest-signing-key, served at GET /v1/reference-values and kept in the reference-values container as {environment}/{sequence}.jws and {environment}/latest.jws. It lists the workloads, transport keys and tls-key versions clients may trust. Manifests for environments other than dev also carry what rebuilds the release from source.

environment.description: The environment, as its workers' ENVIRONMENT names it.

sequence.description: Higher in every manifest the environment publishes. Clients remember the highest they have seen and refuse lower ones.

not_before.description: Clients refuse the manifest before this time.

not_after.description: Clients refuse the manifest from this time on.

claim_sets.description: A worker is approved if its MAA token matches every claim of one set, with its host data among those the set lists.

transport.description: The approved transport key versions. Clients seal uploads only to a listed key. Workers open uploads sealed to their current version and to every listed version with a version, which they release it by.

kid.description: The key's RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint: SHA-256, unpadded base64url.

spki_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the key's DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, padded base64.

images.description: The image digests the approved policies were generated from.

tools.description: The versions of the tools that generated the approved policies.

provenance.description: Where the approved release comes from.

commit.description: The git commit the release was built from; dev manifests signed outside a checkout say dev.

nix_output.description: The Nix store path of the image.

layers.description: The dm-verity root hash of each image layer, in order.

timestamp.description: UTC, to the second, in RFC 3339 form.

claim_set.description: Claims as MAA tokens carry them for a confidential container group. Clients check every claim a set names, so a set can't name one they don't check.

authority.description: The MAA endpoint that signs the tokens, as their iss: https, or plain http on loopback in dev.

x-ms-sevsnpvm-hostdata.description: The approved host data, each the SHA-256 of an approved CCE policy. A rollout lists the current and the next.
